calls.head: Depth vs. Star power
calls.body: The Flyers roll four lines, but the Oilers lean on their top six. Philadelphia is near the top of the league for depth, and Edmonton is the worst. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Flyers.

PHI.head: We had Philadelphia as slight underdogs (44%), and it went Edmonton’s way.

EDM.head: We leaned Edmonton’s way (56%), and they came through.

surprises.head: Tristan Jarry stole one
surprises.body: Jarry allowed 2 goals on 36 shots, worth 6.0 expected goals: 4.0 fewer than expected. That is more than Edmonton’s winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 600 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

surprises.head: Edmonton’s power play was at its best
surprises.body: Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years. Even by those standards, this was a big night: 20.8 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 9.3 (about 9.0 against Philadelphia) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 70 games.

surprises.head: Edmonton won against the run of play
surprises.body: With chances like these, Philadelphia would win about 78 games in 100. Edmonton won anyway.

story.head: Hyman reaches 500 points as the Oilers beat the Flyers
paras: Leon Draisaitl opened the scoring for the Oilers on the power play midway through the first, and Vasily Podkolzin made it 2-0 on the power play later in the period. Zach Hyman extended the lead to 3-0 late in the period, his 500th NHL point. Cole Knuble and Noah Cates scored just under five minutes apart in the second half of the second to cut Edmonton’s lead to 3-2, but they got no closer. Draisaitl scored his 20th of the season early in the third to make it 4-2 for the Oilers. Connor McDavid added an empty-net goal with just over a minute left to make it 5-2. Two players had three-point nights: McDavid with a goal and two assists, and Draisaitl with two goals and an assist.

The score flatters the Oilers: the Flyers had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Flyers win about four in five. Tristan Jarry made the difference in net, stopping 34 of 36. Dan Vladař stopped 16 of 19 for the Flyers.
The Oilers killed all eight Flyers power plays. The Oilers moved to 16-3-3 and climbed into first in the NHL in points, while the Flyers dropped to 6-11-6, sixth in the Metropolitan.
